title: Wall Street Lines Up $63 Billion to Finance Broadcom Chips for Anthropic
excerpt: Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley will fund a special purpose vehicle that buys Broadcom XPU accelerators and networking gear and leases them to Anthropic, with deliveries starting in 2027 and Broadcom guaranteeing the senior debt.
body:
• Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion financing on October 26, 2026, to buy Broadcom AI chips and networking gear for Anthropic.
  • A new special purpose vehicle will purchase Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions and lease them to Anthropic, with deliveries expected to start in calendar 2027.
  • Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley are arranging the first-lien financing — about $43.5 billion, or 69% of the total, according to Reuters — while Blackstone is the sole provider of the committed second-lien portion.
  • Broadcom is providing residual value support to the vehicle equal to the first-lien portion, effectively guaranteeing senior lenders against a fall in the value of the hardware.

Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley will provide $63 billion in financing to buy Broadcom's AI chips and networking equipment for Anthropic, the four firms announced on Monday. Reuters described it as one of the largest debt deals tied to the AI buildout. The money does not go to Anthropic as a loan. It flows through a newly formed special purpose vehicle that will own the hardware and lease it to the maker of the Claude AI models.

How the $63 Billion Structure Works

The transaction is part of the strategic compute capacity agreement previously announced by Broadcom, with expected deliveries starting in calendar 2027, the firms said. The special purpose vehicle, backed by committed financing from the four firms, will purchase Broadcom XPU AI accelerators and networking solutions and lease them to Anthropic. That structure keeps the hardware on the vehicle's books while Anthropic pays for the capacity it uses.

The debt is layered. Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley are arranging the first-lien portion, which ranks first if the assets are ever sold. The size of the first-lien, or senior, debt is about $43.5 billion, or 69% of the total financing, according to two sources familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. The announcement itself did not disclose the breakdown of the loans. Blackstone is the sole provider of the committed portion of the second-lien financing, which ranks below the senior debt.

"Fundamentally, the need for AI compute continues to grow at an extraordinary pace. This validates that there is capital available to finance such growth and that Broadcom is uniquely positioned to enable it."

— Hock Tan, President and CEO, Broadcom

Broadcom's Guarantee Sits Behind the Senior Debt

Broadcom is providing residual value support to the vehicle in an amount equivalent to the first-lien portion of the financing. In practice, Reuters reported, that works as a guarantee to senior lenders: Broadcom has agreed to absorb potential declines in the value of the chips and networking assets up to an amount equal to the first-lien debt. Chipmakers have offered similar guarantees in earlier AI infrastructure deals to make large financings workable for lenders.

The support also concentrates risk on Broadcom. Moody's described Broadcom as one of the strongest large technology companies, Reuters reported, but warned that the risk would increase if multiple transactions were undertaken over a short period to meet the sizable funding needs of frontier AI labs.

A Second Large Financing for Anthropic's Compute

This is not the first financing of this kind for Anthropic's Broadcom-based capacity. Apollo and Blackstone had previously agreed to finance a $35 billion expansion of Anthropic's AI computing capacity under an earlier agreement with Broadcom, according to Reuters. Broadcom's backstop in that deal was up to $29 billion, the company said in a filing. The new $63 billion vehicle nearly doubles that earlier package and shows banks and alternative asset managers taking a larger role in paying for AI data-center hardware.

Executives at the financing firms framed the deal as a template for funding compute at scale. "The rapidly growing demand for AI is creating an enormous opportunity to finance compute capacity at scale," said Jon Gray, President and COO of Blackstone. Vis Raghavan, Head of Banking and Executive Vice Chair at Citi, said: "Financing AI demands capital solutions at unprecedented scale."

What Happens Next

Deliveries under the agreement are expected to begin in calendar 2027, so the vehicle's purchases and Anthropic's lease payments will build over time rather than landing at once. Kirkland & Ellis is advising Blackstone, Latham & Watkins is advising Bank of America, Citi and Morgan Stanley, and Sullivan & Cromwell is advising Broadcom, with Evercore as Broadcom's financial advisor. The announcement came on the same day Anthropic publicly unveiled its filing for an initial public offering, according to Dow Jones Newswires. For now, the unanswered questions are commercial: how quickly Anthropic can put the leased capacity to work, and whether the hardware retains enough value to keep Broadcom's residual support from being called on.
